_comment: Single source of truth for the oMLX admin console's design tokens. The web console and the macOS app both read the generated artifacts, never this file directly. Regenerate with `python omlx/admin/build_tokens.py`; CI drift is caught by tests/test_generated_tokens.py.
_exemptions: Values that deliberately stay literals, declared here so the exemption is a decision and not an omission. (1) The cluster fabric's own palette: dashboard.css's cluster block (the `.cluster-fabric*`, `.cluster-v2-tensor-segment*` and strategy-picker rules, lines 302-1050) composites its own greys, and its off-scale weights (550/650/680/750) stay in that block — the group below names them as-is so the values exist as tokens; the block itself is out of scope for this sweep. (2) `layout.railStackBelow` (900px): a media-query prelude cannot read a `var()`, so components.css repeats the literal 900px beside the generated `--settings-rail-stack-below`; the two are pinned together by tests. (3) The decorative gradient/glow layers — the blur-3xl glow behind the login card (login.html:41) and the one behind the dashboard shell (dashboard.html:23): their blur radius, size and opacity are decoration; their colour stop is a `from-neutral-*` utility, which tailwind.config.js does map. (4) Arbitrary values typed in markup (`h-[300px]`, `tracking-[0.3em]`, `rounded-[2px]`, `text-[12px]` …) are literals by construction: the resolver-level wiring cannot reach them without rewriting markup, which this series forbids.
_paperOnly: Declared, untouched, and reported rather than wired or deleted: typography.floor (--fs-floor*, no reader), console.duration.slow (no reader — the utility-facing 300ms key is console.duration.300, so slow keeps its value and stays unread), and material.topBarBlur/topBarSaturate (--topbar-blur/--topbar-saturate, read only by generated rules).

surface._comment: The page's own plane and the materials drawn on it. `bgPrimary` is the fill a card, sheet or drawer wears; `bgSecondary` and `bgTertiary` step away from it for headers, wells and controls; the two `border*` values are the hairline pair. `fillRaised` is the layer *above* `bgPrimary` — a popover, the command palette, a toast, a selected row, a segmented knob: something sitting on a surface rather than on the page. In the light appearance it is the same white as `bgPrimary`, because the light ramp has no separate raised step; in the dark appearance being raised becomes a colour, one step above `bgTertiary`. `bgStrong` is the step `bg-neutral-200` renders today: one full step below `bgTertiary` in the light appearance (#e5e5e5, so a hover on a secondary well keeps its affordance instead of collapsing into the well it sits on), and the same #2d2d32 as `bgTertiary` in the dark one — where the old override already sent it, so the night pixels do not move.

control._comment: Filled controls. `primary` stays the neutral high-contrast fill (a segmented control's chosen knob, a switch-like plate); `accent` is the console's one filled action colour, and it is the same near-black as `primary` (`#171717`, what the console drew before the token layer and what the project still ships on the branch this series targets): a button that saves and a button that acts wear the same weight, and the blue in the palette stays the *interaction* tint (`semantic.accent` — links, a selected row), never a fill. Hover always moves away from the label's contrast, never below it. `focusRing` is the console's own black: the same value the filled action colour uses in each appearance (`#171717` in the light one, `#e5e5e5` in the dark one), so a keyboard ring reads as part of the palette rather than a tint from outside it; it is a mark rather than text, so 3:1 is the bar. `switchOn` is the black the console already drew in the light appearance and one grey step in the dark one (`#a1a1aa`), so an on switch stays a mark instead of a hole in its track; the knob's position already carries the state, so the fill is a second signal rather than the only one. `onFill` is the fixed white that reads on a fill that stays dark in both appearances — badges, tooltips, dark segments: it is what `text-white` resolves to in tailwind.config.js, because `text-white` shares Tailwind's single `colors` key with the `bg-white` surface and one mapping cannot serve both (the surface resolves through the `.bg-white` companion rule instead).

semantic._comment: Apple system colors, expressed per appearance so the web console reads the same weight as the native app's status dots. `accent` is the console's one tint — the system blue the HIG tints controls with — and it is what the chat's composer, the settings rail's selected section and every link and focus ring now draw. The other six are status marks only: dots, bars, badges. Nothing decorative is coloured. `teal` and `purple` are here for the log levels the app also draws (see dashboard.js logLevelTone): six levels, six marks, one meaning each.

typography._comment: Six levels, no others. Nothing may render below the auxiliary step (12px); the enhanced-readability switch now only raises contrast, because the floor it used to enforce is the floor of the scale itself.

families.sans: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', 'PingFang SC', 'Hiragino Sans GB', 'Noto Sans CJK SC', 'Microsoft YaHei', sans-serif
families.mono: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, 'SF Mono', Menlo, Consolas, monospace

aux.usage: captions, timestamps, table secondary cells, badges

body.usage: body copy, form labels, table primary cells

section.usage: section headings, drawer and sheet titles

leading._comment: The four `leading-*` utilities the markup uses, at the exact ratios they render today (a line-height may not move). They are deliberately not the scale's ratios — the scale belongs to the six type levels, these belong to single-line labels, dense copy and loose paragraphs — so they live beside the scale rather than in it.

fontWeight._comment: 100-800 for the `font-*` utilities, plus the four off-scale weights the hand-written CSS invents (550/650/680/750), tokenised exactly as they are — never normalised onto the scale. The off-scale readers all live in dashboard.css's cluster block, which is exempt from this sweep (see `_exemptions`), so those four exist as tokens first and gain readers when the fabric is next touched.

letterSpacing._comment: The four `tracking-*` utilities at today's exact em values, plus `caps` — the 0.06em the uppercase captions in components.css type by hand. `tracking-[0.3em]` is an arbitrary value in markup and stays a literal (see `_exemptions`).

opacity._comment: The `opacity-*` steps in use, unitless as opacity must be. Keys are the utility's own numbers (50 → 0.5), so `opacity-50` and the stylesheet's `opacity: 0.5` read the same token.

space._comment: 8pt grid. 4pt exists only for icon-to-label gaps — the eight grid keys (1,2,3,4,5,6,8,10 → 4,8,12,16,24,32,48,64) never move. The keys added for the Tailwind wiring are the pixel value they name (20 → 20px, 28 → 28px …), except the three sub-grid steps whose bare numbers are already grid steps (2, 6, 10 mean 8/32/64 here), so their pixels carry a `px` suffix (2px → 2px). Name collisions with Tailwind's scale are resolved by value, never by number: in tailwind.config.js `space-1..4` map to `--space-1..4` (equal pixels), `space-5` (20px) → `--space-20`, `space-6` (24px) → `--space-5`, `space-7` (28px) → `--space-28`, `space-8` (32px) → `--space-6`, `space-9` (36px) → `--space-36`, `space-10` (40px) → `--space-40`, `space-11` (44px) → `--space-44`, `space-12` (48px) → `--space-8`, `space-14` (56px) → `--space-56`, `space-16` (64px) → `--space-10`, and `space-20…96` → `--space-80…384`: every utility keeps the pixels it renders today.

radius._comment: sm/md/lg/pill are the components.css vocabulary (32 refs) and keep their values; 2/4/16/24 are the pixel values `rounded-sm`, `rounded`, `rounded-2xl` and `rounded-3xl` render today. Tailwind's names and these names collide on purpose and are mapped by pixel equality in tailwind.config.js: `rounded-md` (6px) → `--radius-sm`, `rounded-lg` (8px) → `--radius-md`, `rounded-xl` (12px) → `--radius-lg`, and `rounded-full` (9999px) → `--radius-pill` (999px) — the same rendered shape for every element the console draws, because a corner radius clamps at half the shorter side and nothing the console paints is 1998px on its short edge.

layout._comment: Grid metrics that are part of the layout scale rather than page-local numbers: the console measure, the KPI card minimum width, the heatmap label column, the log viewer columns, row pitch and the height its occurrence list scrolls in, and the settings anchor rail. There is exactly one measure and every page shares it: `widths` is the set the Status tab's layout control offers, `default` is the console's measure out of the box, and the chosen one is applied to the page frame itself — so a wider dashboard widens Settings, Logs, Models and Bench with it. `0` means no limit. `topBarHeight`, `subTabHeight` and `stickyGap` are the three numbers the sticky layers are built from, measured at the default type scale. The page scrolls the window, so a sticky sub-tab row pins at `top: topBarHeight` (right below the top bar), a sticky rail below it at `stickyOffset` = `topBarHeight + subTabHeight + stickyGap`, and a section anchor -- also positioned against the viewport -- clears the same `stickyOffset`.

material._comment: Two translucent layers only: the top bar and the modal scrim. Content surfaces stay solid.

elevation._comment: Micro shadows replace hard borders on cards and popovers. `default/sm/md/lg/xl/2xl` are Tailwind's own shadow values, copied verbatim so `shadow-*` utilities resolve through a token without moving a pixel; the dark overrides in dashboard.css that give these shadows a heavier night weight are kept beside them, because one value per key cannot be two weights.

badge._comment: Badge foregrounds. A tone badge is the system colour at 14% behind its label, which is far too light to carry text, so each appearance names the step that reaches 4.5:1 on its own tint (the console contrast suite measures it). The system colours stay for dots, bars and fills. One tone per log level, so the label and the colour never disagree.

console._comment: Web console only: transition durations and the two overlay widths. The app animates with its own timings, so these never reach DesignTokens.swift. The numeric keys are the `duration-*` utilities' milliseconds, merged into this group rather than kept beside it: 200ms is `normal`, and `100/150/500/700` name themselves. `slow` (300ms) is paper-only — see `_paperOnly` — so the utility-facing 300ms step is its own key, `300`, and slow keeps its value with no reader.

notice._comment: Banner fills and borders: the amber tone warns, the red tone reports a failure. Both appearances name the same values, like the label colours beside them, because the Tailwind literals they replace did not change with the appearance either. `.notice--orange` / `.notice--red` in components.css are the only readers.

label._comment: Label colours: the tags and chips that are not log levels — a model profile, a preset, a model type, a cluster state. Each family is a fill plus the step that reaches 4.5:1 on it. These started as Tailwind literals in the markup, which a theme cannot reach; naming them here is what lets the custom-theme feature recolour them. Both appearances name the same values, because the literals they replace did not change with the appearance either.
